description: Integrate the citation anchor, re-capture the baseline, then land F-1: meta-catalog-sync carries the Graph status structurally and states a `reason` on ALL FIVE applied:0 arms. This FEAT must come first for two independent reasons. (1) The worktree is 12 commits behind origin/stack = 061b6e77, which is the commit every file:line in design.md and plan.md is relative to; four of the files later FEATs edit differ between the two, so their line numbers are wrong until the merge lands, and F-4's seventh site does not even exist at the current HEAD. (2) design.md 5 carries a BINDING ordering constraint: F-1 touches no shared module, so it must be the only change in the tree at any publish time - every shared-package change (F-4, F-5, F-6) lands after it, never before, or a fleet-wide publisher would sweep F-1's target. Corresponds to plan.md Part A items 1 and 2. Target function: wecare-meta-catalog-sync. The DEPLOY is OWNER CONFIRM (O10), plan.md Part B row B1 - do not deploy.
steps: STEP 1 - integrate the anchor. Run `git -C <worktree> fetch origin` then `git rev-parse origin/stack`. If it is still 061b6e77c8a352d174c713834af0ca7d61b027b9, proceed. If it has MOVED, you must merge the new tip and then re-derive EVERY `git grep -n` anchor named in plan.md items 2 through 8 at the new base before any later FEAT touches code - record the move and the re-derived numbers in this FEAT's findings. Integrate with `git -C <worktree> merge origin/stack`. NEVER `git rebase` and NEVER `--force`. The merge was verified clean at planning time (`git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/stack` exits 0, no conflict). If git nevertheless reports a conflict, resolve it in favour of origin/stack for every file OUTSIDE .kiro/work/deep-integration-audit/ and never discard the parallel session's content.

STEP 2 - re-capture both baselines on the merged tree and write the numbers into this FEAT's findings and into plan.md under a 'post-merge baseline' note. Whole suite: `cd <worktree> && <venv-python> -m pytest -q`. Focused: the same command with `tests/test_meta_catalog_sync_handler.py tests/test_meta_catalog_sync.py tests/test_paid_vault.py tests/test_paid_submit_request.py tests/test_dropdocs_vault_no_second_charge.py`. Pre-merge reference: 10342 passed / 6 skipped / 3 xfailed whole-suite, 161 passed focused. The post-merge count must be >= 10342; every later FEAT compares against the post-merge number.

STEP 3 - re-derive F-1's anchors on the merged tree before editing: `git grep -n 'raise RuntimeError' -- amplify/functions/ecommerce/meta-catalog-sync/handler.py` (it is the ONLY one in the file, which is what makes errorType a reliable localiser), `git grep -n 'meta_catalog_sync_read_failed' -- <same>`, `git grep -n '"applied": 0' -- <same>`. Expected at the anchor: the raise at :233, the log at :554-557, and applied:0 arms at :528-529, :558-559, :568-572, :599-601, :604-606.

STEP 4 - add the structural exception to amplify/functions/ecommerce/meta-catalog-sync/handler.py at module level: `class MetaCatalogReadError(RuntimeError)` with a docstring saying it carries the Graph status structurally and never a body. Model it on amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/wix_ecom.py:59-75 (status readable as .status, never parsed out of prose). Note that module is at lambda_utils/wix_ecom.py, NOT under lambda_utils/ecommerce/.

STEP 5 - raise it at :233 in place of the bare RuntimeError, setting .status from result['error'].get('status') and .errorKind from result['error'].get('type') (the latter for the non-HTTPError transport case). Keep the message. MetaCatalogReadError subclasses RuntimeError, so type(e).__name__ stays a reliable localiser and becomes MORE specific.

STEP 6 - add `graphStatus` and `graphErrorKind` to the existing meta_catalog_sync_read_failed log line at :554-557 AND NOTHING ELSE. The Graph RESPONSE BODY must still never be logged - :208-209 records why: the body echoes the request, whose one header is a credential. Only the integer status and the exception class name may be added. The fail-closed behaviour is unchanged: a read failure still returns reason 'read_failed' and still constructs no write request.

STEP 7 - make `reason` total over the applied:0 return surface. :568-572 (the readOnly inspect readback) gains "reason": "read_only_inspect". :599-601 gains "reason": "disabled" if not enabled else "dry_run" - DERIVED, not hard-coded, because that one arm covers both the disabled and the dry-run case and does not distinguish them today. :604-606 (empty plan) gains "reason": "nothing_to_apply". Leave :528-529 ('unconfigured') and :558-559 ('read_failed') alone - they already have one. Leave the :534 batchHandle arm alone - it has no `applied` key at all and is out of scope.

STEP 8 - write the four regression tests in the EXISTING tests/test_meta_catalog_sync_handler.py (29 tests today), reusing its rig: the `run(wix, graph, reader=None, event=None)` helper (anchor on `def run(`, currently :180), `FakeGraph` (:139) and `reader_for` (:168). (a) test_a_read_failure_reports_the_graph_status - FakeGraph(error={'status': 403}); assert the captured meta_catalog_sync_read_failed record has graphStatus == 403, out['reason'] == 'read_failed', graph.writes == [], and that NO value in the record contains 'Bearer' or 'FAKE_TOKEN'. (b) test_a_transport_failure_reports_the_kind_and_no_status - FakeGraph(error={'type': 'URLError'}); assert graphErrorKind present and graphStatus is None. (c) test_every_applied_zero_arm_states_its_reason - parametrised over all five arms, asserting reason is present and equal to unconfigured / read_failed / read_only_inspect / disabled / dry_run / nothing_to_apply as appropriate. (d) confirm the existing test_a_META_read_failure_does_not_become_a_write still passes UNCHANGED - it is the sensitivity proof.

STEP 9 - LOG-CAPTURE MECHANISM, because this file has no caplog precedent (all 29 existing tests assert on return values only). The handler binds `logger = get_logger(__name__)` at :57; lambda_utils.logging.get_logger (logging.py:17) only calls logging.getLogger(name) and setLevel, adds no handler and never sets propagate = False, so records reach the root logger that caplog attaches to. Take the logger name FROM THE MODULE OBJECT, never a hardcoded guess - the rig loads the handler by path under MODULE_NAME = 'wecare_meta_catalog_sync_handler': use `caplog.set_level(logging.ERROR, logger=handler_module.logger.name)`. get_logger applies LOG_LEVEL (default INFO) at setLevel, so a test asserting on an INFO record must either leave LOG_LEVEL unset or set caplog.set_level on the SAME logger - the level on the logger, not the handler, is what filters. DO NOT put these tests in tests/test_meta_catalog_sync.py: its test_the_module_is_pure_at_import and test_the_module_logs_nothing_at_all assert properties a log-capturing, handler-driving test sits badly beside.

STEP 10 - run the focused tests and SEE THE NEW ONES FAIL FIRST if you wrote them before the source change (graphStatus does not exist today; three of the five arms have no reason). Then confirm they pass. Then run the whole suite.

STEP 11 - commit. Two commits are acceptable here and preferred: one for the merge (git merge creates it), one for F-1 with its tests. Stage EXACT paths only - amplify/functions/ecommerce/meta-catalog-sync/handler.py and tests/test_meta_catalog_sync_handler.py. NEVER `git add .` / `-A` / `-u` and never `git commit -a`. Do not push.

STEP 12 - set this FEAT's status to completed and record in findings: the post-merge whole-suite and focused counts, whether origin/stack moved, and any citation line number that differed from plan.md's value on the merged tree (later FEATs depend on this).
